title: When Wording Steers the Evaluation: Framing Bias in LLM judges
reasoning: The paper investigates 'framing bias' (a linguistic/psychological effect) in LLM-based evaluation across four tasks: truthfulness, jailbreak detection, toxicity detection, and grammatical acceptability. While jailbreak and toxicity detection have safety implications, the paper's focus is on the reliability and consistency of the judge models rather than evaluating or benchmarking religion, morals, or specific ethical frameworks.
